attribution.note: Curve values are derived from Kalshi event-contract market data, which remains subject to Kalshi’s terms.

note: The first value is an instrument-specific anchor: a future exact-time weekly implied median when a usable weekly ladder exists, otherwise the front-month monthly-average implied median (identified per chip in anchors). Remaining values are monthly-average tenors. Each implied level is the strike where a ladder’s yes-probability crosses 50%, and the resting bids and asks bracket it: a bid at one strike is a floor on every lower strike’s probability and an ask a ceiling on every higher one, so the bid-only and ask-only envelopes each cross 50% somewhere. The bracket is those two crossings, each interpolated linearly between the listed strikes around it; strictly, the quotes bound the median only to the outer of those strikes. A side no quote bounds is open. The level reads only usable quotes: a strike with a bid above 0¢ and an ask below 100¢ counts as two-sided, but is read at its midpoint only when no wider than 20 points with size on both sides, and a strike without such a quote only at a last trade with 24-hour volume. A weighted isotonic fit (pool-adjacent violators, each quote weighted by its tightness) keeps them monotone — it can raise a level as well as lower it, unlike a running minimum — and nothing is smoothed: each monthly value is its own ladder’s estimate. With fewer than two usable quotes, or a fit that never crosses 50% within its own strikes or crosses it outside the bracket, no quote sets the level: a closed bracket gives its midpoint, and an open one only a placeholder (its closed side, or the middle of the listed strikes when neither side is closed) that the site never shows as a price — it shows the bracket. In this snapshot 4 of 50 ladders are read from their fit of 23 usable quotes, and 31 brackets are open on at least one side. A point passes — it is identified — only with both sides of its bid/ask bracket inside the listed strikes, a bracket no wider than 20% of its median, and at least 2 two-sided strikes, 1¢/99¢ placeholders excluded, quoted between 20% and 80%; 3 of 55 points pass this snapshot, and 24 of the snapshot’s 137 two-sided strikes are 1¢/99¢ placeholders. Only identified points draw a line and a band, and only they feed moves, carry, spreads and curve shapes. Quality is reported per point. These are reconstructed market-implied levels, not current spot or executable quotes.
